clue.text: Sophisticated know Telegraph should provide material that's often on the edge

definitions.text: material that's often on the edge

parts.note: chic means stylish and sophisticated
ken is knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'; here read as the verb to know
to wire is to send a telegram, so to telegraph

explanation.surface: A boast that this newspaper will supply edgy material, Telegraph being the paper the puzzle appears in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telegraph' looks like the newspaper but is the verb, giving WIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken wire is light mesh netting, often used to fence the edges of gardens and runs.

clue.text: Shy men lose their heads over a catlike creature

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above what follows
the heads of the two words shy and men are their first letters, which are dropped

explanation.surface: Timid men are decapitated by some feline beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping S and M leaves HY and EN; A follows below.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyenas look somewhat feline and belong to the cat-like branch of carnivores, though they are not cats.

clue.text: Doctor of mercy to get medicinal herb

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of these words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A merciful physician prescribes a herbal remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a noun but is a verb signalling the rearrangement of OF MERCY.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfrey is a plant long used in folk medicine to heal bruises and broken bones.

clue.text: Scheme, extreme elements of Euroscepticism are first to take on

indicators.note: are first says these letters come before the next piece
the extreme elements of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: a ploy is a scheme or stratagem

explanation.surface: A political plot by Eurosceptic extremists to seize power first.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ someone is to hire them, which is to take them on as staff.

clue.text: Maybe Stork's spread?

parts.note: Stork is a brand of margarine, a spread, but read the bird's spread: how far its outstretched wings reach

explanation.surface: A query about margarine: is Stork a spread?
explanation.walkthrough: Stork is a well-known British margarine brand; the capital S misleads, as the clue means the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's span from wingtip to wingtip is how far it spreads its wings.

clue.text: Witter on about replacing a British dish

indicators.note: replacing says one piece swaps in for another inside the word

parts.note: to rabbit, or rabbit on, is British slang for chattering, like to witter on
B is the abbreviation for British; a says just one B is swapped
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone chatters on about swapping out a traditional British dish.
explanation.walkthrough: RABBIT has two Bs; one goes and RE takes its place. Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit, usually Welsh rarebit, is a dish of melted cheese sauce on toast.

clue.text: Crooks half escaping — CID and police baffled about law to begin with — one is on a lead?

indicators.note: with half the word escaping, only its first half is kept
about says the jumbled letters go round the next piece
baffled means confused, so these letters are jumbled
to begin with means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Crooks evade capture while baffled detectives think about the law, and someone is kept on a lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the shuffled detectives and police round the law's opening letter. The 'lead' is an electrical wire, not a dog's leash.
explanation.definitionFit: A crocodile clip is a toothed spring clip fixed to the end of an electrical wire.

clue.text: Disapproved of a Lego product making uniform base colour

indicators.note: making says one letter is turned into another

parts.note: Duplo is the brand of large toy bricks made by Lego
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
e is the base of natural logarithms
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Building something from Lego with a uniform-coloured base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making uniform base' changes the U in DUPLO to E, giving DEPLO.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplore something is to condemn it strongly, so the past tense is disapproved of.

clue.text: Poet raged about everything with article and detailed verse

indicators.note: about means around or astir, so these letters move

parts.note: all means everything
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: detailed means the tail, the final letter, is cut off

parts.note: a poem is a piece of verse

explanation.surface: A furious poet rails against the whole lot, writing verse with every detail.
explanation.walkthrough: Detailed means de-tailed: POEM loses M. The grid prints ALLEN, but the wordplay gives AN and the poet spelt his middle name Allan.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was the American writer of The Raven and many other poems.

clue.text: Rod Hull initially restitched Emu's tears

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each word
restitched means sewn back together differently, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the puppet's name gives its three letters; the 's only joins it to tears

explanation.surface: Rod Hull mends his puppet Emu, which had been weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod Hull was a British entertainer whose act was a violent puppet emu.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose; in poetry it means tears.

clue.text: Correspondent and prison priest dine out

parts.note: pen is slang for prison, short for penitentiary
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A letter writer, a prison chaplain, goes out to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen friend is someone you exchange letters with, so a correspondent.

clue.text: Locate right page in stomach churning online forums

indicators.note: locate, together with in, says one piece is set inside the other
in, together with locate, says where the piece is placed
a churning stomach is one turned over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ro is short for recto, the right-hand page of an open book

explanation.surface: Instructions to find the right page while your stomach is churning.
explanation.walkthrough: Books print the right-hand page as recto, abbreviated ro; 'Locate ... in' is a split container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chat rooms are websites where users hold discussions with one another, a kind of internet forum.

clue.text: Oddly, boat lost a raft

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Strangely, a boat lost one of its rafts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like an adverb for strangeness; it picks out the odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is the Spanish word for a raft, used in English for a light South American raft or fishing boat.

clue.text: Draws crowd at last — starts to erupt, 'Come on you Spurs'

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of the word
starts to means the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A football crowd erupts with a chant for Tottenham Hotspur.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoy lures, so to decoy is to draw something in; decoys is a verb meaning draws.

clue.text: Last hint to describe where you'll find Blue coats put together with no frills

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so this piece goes around the other

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or hint

indicators.note: with no frills means the outer letters are trimmed off

parts.note: Pontins holiday camps are staffed by entertainers called Bluecoats

explanation.surface: Seemingly an awkward lead-in to blue coats being joined without frills.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontins is a British holiday-camp chain whose entertainers are called Bluecoats. 'put together' is only link glue.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to go on, endure or carry on without stopping.

clue.text: Bugs found in hair etc — a bride's revolting

indicators.note: revolting says the hidden letters are read backwards
found in says the letters are tucked inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something nasty has been discovered in a bride's hair and other things.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Bugs found' as the definition, but 'found in' is what signals the hidden letters, so the definition is just 'Bugs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs is an informal word for germs or microbes, which bacteria are.

clue.text: Something you shouldn't put in a car — wasting energy is unethical

indicators.note: wasting means losing or giving up, so a letter is removed

parts.words: Something you shouldn't put in a car
parts.note: the wrong fuel, petrol in a diesel or the reverse, should never go in a car
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Putting the wrong thing in a car wastes energy, and that is immoral.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongful means unjust or unlawful, which is close to unethical.

clue.text: Secure Wahlberg, say, for feature

parts.note: to land something is to secure it, as in landing a job
Mark Wahlberg is an American actor, so his first name is an example of what Wahlberg gives

explanation.surface: Signing up the actor Wahlberg for a feature film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' suggests a film; it is a prominent feature of a landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A landmark is a prominent, recognisable feature of a place.

clue.text: Everything inside small dark vial showing disease

indicators.note: everything inside a word is all its letters except the first and last

explanation.surface: A tiny dark vial contains a sample of disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everything' tempts as ALL; here it means all the inner letters of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaria is a fever spread by mosquitoes, carrying a parasite of the blood.

clue.text: Hooligan caught by CCTV and alarm

indicators.note: caught by says the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A thug is filmed on security cameras and sets off an alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal is someone who wantonly damages property, a kind of yob or hooligan.

clue.text: Obey orders and carry on working

parts.note: to carry on is to misbehave or make a fuss, which is to act up
on means working or operating, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: Do as you're told and keep going at your job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carry on' reads as continue, but it means misbehave. You act upon orders, so the definition takes 'orders' with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To act upon instructions is to follow them, so acting upon orders means complying with them.

clue.text: A male, perhaps on the radio programme

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard spoken, so a word is replaced by one that sounds like it

parts.note: male is an example of a gender

explanation.surface: A man, it seems, is broadcasting on a radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech, GENDER and GENDA sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a programme or schedule of things to be done.

clue.text: Scare companion sick

parts.note: CH is short for Companion of Honour, a British order
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A sick friend gets a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: To chill someone is to frighten them, as in a chilling tale.

clue.text: Wee Willie Winkie's bedtime habit

parts.note: the nursery-rhyme boy runs through the town in his night attire; habit means clothing, not a routine

explanation.walkthrough: Wee Willie Winkie is a nursery rhyme figure who 'runs through the town, upstairs and downstairs' in his nightwear. 'Habit' suggests a routine but means a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme dresses him in a long loose garment worn in bed, his habit as clothing.

clue.text: Every now and then locals miss a watering-hole

indicators.note: every now and then means taking letters at regular intervals, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Pub regulars sometimes skip a visit to their local bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watering-hole' suggests a pub, set up by 'locals'; it is a desert spring.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert with water, a natural watering place.

clue.text: Drug high involved bonfire outside

indicators.note: outside says the jumbled letters sit around the other piece
involved means tangled or complicated, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: up means high, as in up in the air

explanation.surface: Someone is high on drugs at a bonfire party.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled bonfire letters split around the high piece, so 'outside' is a container signal, not a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a common painkilling and anti-inflammatory medicine.

clue.text: Instruction to reader to preserve drained excess sauce

indicators.note: to preserve something is to keep it held inside, so the other piece goes within

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, is printed at the foot of a page for the reader

indicators.note: drained means emptied of its contents, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Cooking directions about preserving sauce after draining the excess.
explanation.walkthrough: PTO, please turn over, is the note at a page foot telling the reader to go on; 'drained' leaves only the outer letters of 'excess'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts, garlic, cheese and oil.

clue.text: Polish conjuror finally involved in perfect disappearance

parts.note: to nail something is to get it perfectly right

indicators.note: involved in says one letter is caught up inside the other word

parts.note: a vanish is a magician's trick of making something disappear

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A magician perfects a vanishing act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' at the start hides its lower-case sense: it is a cosmetic, not the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Nail varnish is a lacquer painted on fingernails, also called nail polish.
